blogs.title: Not All Neck Swelling Is Angioedema: Spotting Dermatomyositis Pseudoangioedema in the ED
blogs.description: A practical approach to atraumatic neck swelling that doesn’t behave like histaminergic or bradykinin-mediated angioedema. We highlight bedside clues (afebrile course, prolonged time course, subtle periungual changes, rashes), pitfalls (normal C1-INH/C4 does not end the workup), and the single lab that changes the trajectory—early creatine kinase with AST/ALT interpretation for muscle source. Includes a streamlined algorithm for adding myositis to the differential and avoiding delays in immunosuppression.

blogs.title: Bulbar Myositis Playbook: Dysphagia, Aspiration, and Airway in Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: How to recognize and manage bulbar involvement in inflammatory myopathy: interpreting a “messy” flexible nasendoscopy, ordering videofluoroscopy early, and using NG feeding to protect the lungs. We outline supportive care to reduce aspiration risk, when to pulse steroids, and why IVIG is often prioritized in dysphagia-dominant disease. Practical tips on monitoring recovery and timing return to oral intake.

blogs.title: Decoding Anti-SAE1 Dermatomyositis: Phenotype, Risks, and What It Means at the Bedside
blogs.description: A clinician’s guide to the anti-SAE1 antibody: expected skin phenotype, high rates of dysphagia and interstitial lung disease, and a nontrivial malignancy signal. We discuss where SAE1 fits among myositis-specific antibodies, how to interpret line-blot positivity in context, and why this case—prominent neck pseudoangioedema—pushes us to widen the phenotype we consider. Actionable implications for counseling, monitoring, and treatment planning.

blogs.title: CT, MRI, PET, and the Biopsy: Imaging and Path Pearls that Separate Myositis from Deep Neck Infection
blogs.description: When CT shows strap muscle and retropharyngeal edema without a drainable source, think beyond infection. We review imaging patterns that favor inflammatory myopathy, the role of MRI to map activity, and how FDG-PET can simultaneously stage muscle disease and screen for malignancy. Pathology clinchers—perifascicular injury and capillary C5b-9 deposition—tie the diagnosis together and prevent unnecessary ENT interventions.

blogs.title: Hitting Hard and Early: Building an Immunosuppressive Strategy for Severe Dermatomyositis with Dysphagia
blogs.description: A stepwise regimen for high-risk presentations: pulse methylprednisolone, rapid transition to a slow prednisone taper, early IVIG for bulbar disease, and selecting a steroid-sparing agent (why many favor mycophenolate when lung involvement is a concern). We discuss when to add rituximab, CK and function-based monitoring, and PJP prophylaxis options when trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole isn’t tolerated (e.g., inhaled pentamidine).

blogs.title: Dermatomyositis and Cancer: How to Operationalize the IMACS Screening Guideline
blogs.description: Translating IMACS risk stratification to the bedside: identifying high-risk features (e.g., dermatomyositis with dysphagia, male sex, antibody profile), choosing first-line tests (CT, PET where appropriate), and when to add endoscopy. We cover surveillance intervals after a negative initial screen, how to integrate evolving symptoms, and communicating risk while avoiding over-testing.
